question_text: A transit operator trains an ML scheduling model on vehicle locations linked to drivers. Discuss one benefit and one ethical risk of keeping detailed location histories.
adaptation_rationale: Retains tracking-data ethics while explicitly supplying ML training context; only adapted A4.4.1 coverage is claimed.
solution: Historical patterns may train more accurate delay predictions and improve scheduling, making service more reliable. However, identifiable histories enable monitoring of drivers beyond what is necessary. Retention limits and purpose restrictions can preserve operational benefits while reducing privacy intrusion.
